title: John Powell claims the island
description: An English captain finds the island uninhabited and claims it for King James I.

title: First English settlement
description: Eighty English settlers land on the west coast, the start of uninterrupted English and then Barbadian society.

title: House of Assembly meets
description: The governor calls an elected assembly that survives as one of the oldest parliaments in the Americas.

title: Treaty of Oistins
description: The island's royalist planters surrender to a Parliamentary fleet in exchange for articles confirming their assembly and lands.

title: Slave code
description: The assembly passes a harsh slave code that becomes the model for other English slave colonies.

title: Slave revolt foiled
description: A planned island-wide slave rising is betrayed days before it is to begin, and scores are executed.

title: Great Hurricane
description: The deadliest known Atlantic hurricane strikes Barbados before killing tens of thousands across the eastern Caribbean.

title: Bussa's rebellion
description: The largest slave revolt in Barbadian history is crushed within days; its leader Bussa becomes a national hero.

title: Confederation riots
description: Planter-led crowds riot against a plan to join a Windward Islands confederation, killing several black protesters.

title: Labour riots
description: The deportation of the labour organiser Clement Payne sets off days of rioting that push the colony toward mass political organisation.

title: First election with universal suffrage
description: The first general election with universal adult suffrage confirms the Barbados Labour Party's dominance.

title: Grantley Adams first premier
description: Grantley Adams becomes the island's first premier under the new constitution.

title: Full internal self-government
description: Errol Barrow's Democratic Labour Party wins the first election after Barbados gains full internal self-government.

title: Independence
description: Barbados becomes an independent state with Errol Barrow as its first prime minister.

title: Tom Adams elected
description: The Barbados Labour Party returns to power under Tom Adams, ending fifteen years of Democratic Labour Party rule.

title: Death of Errol Barrow
description: The first prime minister of independent Barbados dies in office during his final term.

title: Bridgetown named World Heritage
description: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison are inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage list.

title: Mia Mottley first female prime minister
description: Mia Mottley is sworn in after a landslide, becoming the country's first female prime minister.
